app.meta_description: Lightcutoff is a project that aims to collect data on the supply of electrical energy in Cameroon, these data are mainly provided by people directly concerned by these cuts (the population).

about.title: About us
about.content: In Cameroon, access to public resources such as electricity and water is not easy. Some regions may even be deprived of them for several days or even weeks. The {projectTitle} project aims to help make an inventory of the state of the art on the supply of electrical energy in Cameroon. This in order to allow third parties to exploit this data in areas such as research or help in choosing a place to live.

aboutus.title: Who are we?
aboutus.slogan: This is all about the project
aboutus.text_history_1: The story of the project {projectTitle} started with one of the longest power cuts I have experienced since I have been living in Cameroon. I've been living in Yaoundé for a few years now, and I had one of the most disturbing experiences of my life about the power cuts. Indeed, we had no light for several days. Don't be mistaken, light cuts are frequent in my city (my country too) but, for me, this was a first.
aboutus.text_history_2: Unfortunately for me, the cut was very extensive and working from home, I had no way of knowing which areas were affected or not, so I lost several days of work.
aboutus.text_obj_1: The project {projectTitle} on which we are working, aims to help make an inventory of the situation regarding the power cuts throughout the country. This for the purpose of allowing third parties to exploit this data to do research, for example, to be able to travel to work, or even find housing according to the trends of cuts.
aboutus.text_obj_2: Thus, the project {projectTitle} will make it possible to provide the population with information on the supply of electrical energy in the country.
aboutus.text_obj_3: We have great hope that the project will be able to help a large number of people whose activity is governed by the absence or not of electrical energy.

tuto.title_page: Tutorial, learning how to use our tool
tuto.report_alert_2: In this tutorial we consider that a report is also a report, an alert and vice versa.
tuto.report_alert_1: For the moment, {projectTitle} is only available in Cameroon. This means that no report will be accepted if it is made outside Cameroon.
tuto.text_presentation: {projectTitle} a pour objectif d’aider les utilisaturs d'énergie électrique à s’adapter aux contraintes liées aux coupures de courant électrique. Ceci au moyen d'une carte interactive qui leur permettrait de signaler toute coupure ou remise d'énergie électrique à l'endroit où ils se trouvent.
tuto.legend_intro: To begin with, here is the legend of our map.
tuto.legend_text_1: As you can see, there's a specific record for each situation. We have:
tuto.legend_text_2: Marqueur bleu: To report your position on the map.
tuto.legend_text_3: Marqueur rouge: Represents a light cut reported by another user.
tuto.legend_text_4: Marqueur orange:Represents a light cut reported by yourself.
tuto.legend_text_5: Marqueur vert:Represents the end of a cut reported by you or another user.
tuto.cluster_text_1: a cluster is an area with a large number of markers. Depending on the number of markers, we have several types of clusters.
tuto.cluster_text_2: Clusters are classified according to the number of markers in the area. Thus, the order of colors ranges from blue for a relatively small number to purple for a very large number of markers.
tuto.begin_text_1: When you arrive on our map, you will be geolocated and your position will be represented by a blue marker.
tuto.begin_text_2: It is possible that your position is not exactly accurate, so to improve it we have provided a search module that will allow you to better locate yourself in the map.
tuto.begin_text_3: If it turns out that you have to move your blue marker over a very long distance, you don't necessarily have to drag it all the way. A double click on a place on the map will suffice.
tuto.begin_text_4: Pour pouvoir ajouter un rapport, il vous suffit de cliquer une fois sur le votre marqueur bleu et un formulaire apparait. Il vous suffira de choisir une date et une heure correspondante à la coupure.
tuto.report_signal_text_1: After creating a report, there are 2 possibilities:
tuto.report_signal_text_2: Vous signalez une coupure en cours: après avoir enregistré le rapport précédent, un nouveau formulaire vous est présenté mais, vous n'êtes pas dans l'obligation de le remplir. Vous remarquerez un marqueur orange qui signale une coupure en cours que vous avez signalé et que vous seul pouvez signaler fini.
tuto.report_signal_text_3: Pour fermer un rapport de coupure émis, il vous suffit de cliquer sur le marqueur orange correspondant et remplir le formulaire.
tuto.report_signal_text_4: Un autre formulaire vous est proposé pour terminer votre rapport: Juste après que vous ayez crée un rapport, il vous ai proposé un nouveau formulaire. En remplissant et en envoyant ce formulaire, vous opérerez alors à la fermeture du rapport de coupure initié plus tôt.
tuto.after_signal_text_1: After closing an issued report (section: Reporting a power failure), you will see a green marker. To let users know that your previous outage report is no longer valid. The situation has returned to normal (power restored).
